audit_findings.title: The nonlinear IDR claim is not represented coherently in either the numerator or denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: The 494.074579 million denominator includes approximately 10 million GP units beyond the 484.057704 million common units, while the separately allocated 2025 IDR claim was $424 million, equal to 19.2% of the $2.213 billion anchor; removing 10 million units alone would increase per-unit value by approximately 2.1%.
audit_findings.mechanism: The model must either deduct GP and IDR claims from consolidated owner earnings before dividing by common units, or use common-only owner earnings and a common-only diluted denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the general partner holds IDRs, which allow the general partner to receive a higher percentage of quarterly distributions of available cash from operating surplus as additional target levels are met, but may transfer these rights separately from its general partner interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated structural error, although its direction depends on how the unreconciled anchor was constructed. If the anchor is already common-only, including GP units understates common value. If it is consolidated, failing to value the separate nonlinear IDR waterfall overstates common value. The filed $424 million 2025 IDR allocation is large enough to affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $2.213 billion anchor from consolidated net income through all owner-earnings adjustments and allocations; then rerun using either common-only cash flow and common diluted units or consolidated cash flow less explicit forecast GP and IDR distributions.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value begins near the rollover of CQP's protected contract economics
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value represents 47.7%-50.9% of operating PV, approximately $12.6-$17.7 billion, while about 90% of production was contracted for a weighted-average remaining life of approximately 12 years at June 30, 2026; the renewal effect is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Contract expirations affect forecast and terminal OE through renewal fees, utilization, margins and exposure of uncontracted capacity to market pricing.
audit_findings.evidence: Through our SPAs and IPM agreements currently in effect, with approximately 13 years of weighted average remaining life as of December 31, 2025, we have contracted with third parties approximately 85% of the total anticipated production from the Liquefaction Project through the mid-2030s.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved future economic assumption rather than a demonstrated accounting error, but it is material now because roughly half of modeled operating value depends on earnings continuing after the forecast reaches the contract-renewal period. Carrying the 2025 economics into a perpetual-growth terminal value without supported post-renewal margins can overstate value materially.
audit_findings.action: Build a contract-by-contract expiration schedule, model renewal pricing and utilization for the contracted and uncontracted capacity, and rerun the terminal value from a supported post-renewal OE level.

audit_findings.title: The completion-based expansion rerun trigger is too late to capture construction funding
audit_findings.magnitude: CQP spent $99 million on the SPL Expansion Project during the first six months of 2026 and issued $1.75 billion of notes, a disclosed but unquantified portion of whose proceeds funded the limited notice to proceed; remaining equity funding and commitments are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Pre-completion construction payments, guarantees and equity contributions reduce cash available to common holders and may increase interest expense before expansion OE enters the valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: The FID of any expansion projects, including the SPL Expansion Project, will result in additional cash requirements to fund the construction and operations of such projects in excess of our current contractual obligations under executed contracts discussed above, although expansion may be designed to leverage shared infrastructure to reduce the incremental costs of any potential expansion.
audit_findings.explanation: The trigger error is demonstrated: spending began under a binding EPC arrangement before completion, and the latest filing says such spending will continue. The $99 million already spent is reflected in June cash, but future committed outflows are absent from the forecast. Given the project's scale and that only $1.205 billion separates the bull equity value from market capitalization at the supplied price, the omitted funding is reasonably capable of changing the scenario conclusion, although its exact net amount is not filed.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the EPC payment schedule, termination obligations, guarantees, project-financing terms and required CQP equity contributions; rerun at LNTP and each positive FID or binding financing commitment, deducting pre-completion funding while separately modeling any expansion earnings admitted to the perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Unreconciled derivative mark-to-market gains could contaminate owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: The filed 2025 fair-value gain was $732 million, equal to 33.1% of the $2.213 billion anchor; actual contamination is unquantified. If the full amount remained in recurring OE, the proportional base-case operating-PV overstatement would be approximately $10.3 billion, or $20.82 per diluted unit.
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrealized derivative marks enter reported earnings but should be reversed from OE, while physical settlements and realized IPM economics must remain without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, as described in Results of Operations in Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, our net income for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 included $732 million and $388 million of gains, respectively, resulting from changes in the fair values of our derivatives, substantially all of which were related to commodity derivative instruments indexed to international LNG prices, mainly our IPM agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The large noncash gain is demonstrated, but contamination of the supplied anchor remains an unresolved possibility because its reconciliation was not provided. The conditional sensitivity shows that even partial retention could materially alter the valuation. The June 2026 NPNS designation also creates future noncash amortization that will require separate treatment.
audit_findings.action: Produce a year-by-year bridge from GAAP net income to OE showing reversals of unrealized marks, retained physical settlements, realized IPM margins and deferred-NPNS amortization; rerun the valuation if any noncash amount remains in the anchor or historical series.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor precedes a known property-tax cost step-up
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 ad valorem property tax was $29 million, equal to 1.3% of the $2.213 billion anchor; the incremental expense beginning in 2027 is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration of property-tax incentives increases recurring operating cash expense and therefore reduces forecast OE and terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, we have ad valorem legacy property tax incentives secured for the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal that begin to expire starting in 2027, with continuing incentive roll-off thereafter over the longer term.
audit_findings.explanation: The scheduled roll-off is known and falls inside the explicit forecast, so it is not merely a monitoring item. However, the filing states that the increase depends on future tax rates and assessed values and does not quantify the step-up. The current $29 million expense is already within the anchor; the record cannot establish whether the incremental amount is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the incentive-expiration schedule, taxable assessed values, applicable millage rates and remaining credits; calculate annual incremental taxes and rerun OE from 2027 onward.

audit_findings.title: Current interest expense may not represent the cost of refinancing near-term maturities
audit_findings.magnitude: At least $4.85 billion of stated notes mature in 2028-2030. The 2026 issuance of $1.0 billion at 5.35% and $750 million at 6.05% carried approximately $23.9 million more annual gross coupon than the retired $1.5 billion 5.00% notes, equal to 1.1% of the $2.213 billion anchor, before considering the additional $250 million principal, other repayments and issuance costs.
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the DCF uses equity-level OE after interest, refinancing rates, issuance costs and expansion borrowing change forecast OE directly rather than entering through a separate debt-principal deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Our financing costs could increase or future borrowings or equity offerings may be unavailable to us or unsuccessful, which could cause us to be unable to pay or refinance our indebtedness or to fund our other liquidity needs.
audit_findings.explanation: A refinancing reset is no longer hypothetical: higher-coupon notes were issued in 2026. Nevertheless, total debt remained approximately $14.6 billion and first-half interest expense declined from $378 million to $364 million, so that transaction alone does not demonstrate a material valuation error. The rates and amount of refinancing for the remaining 2028-2030 maturities and expansion debt are unresolved, preventing a firm materiality conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Roll every filed maturity through the forecast using the actual 2026 issuances, current amortization, issuance costs and explicit refinancing-rate cases; add expansion debt only when committed and rerun OE under each case.
